content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a [product_name] CPU and an RS232 cable from [product_name]. I'm using [product_name] software version [version_no]. My laptop doesn't have a COM port, so I'm using a USB converter. When I try going online, communication is slow—the pushbutton is pressed, but in the online test, the input changes after 10 seconds. I tried different COM port speeds and adjusted some settings, but communication remains very slow. I saw a post suggesting to use low-numbered COM ports. My USB converter is a Prolific USB with what I believe is an FTDI chip. What could be causing this issue?

Check if the driver for your USB-SERIAL converter is the correct one for your Windows version. Sometimes, problems arise when using 32-bit drivers on a 64-bit system. Also, make sure your Java runtime environment is fully updated. Regarding the converter cable, if it's seen a lot of use, perhaps the copper connectors on the USB side need attention—try bending them outward a bit. Ideally, do you have another cable you can use to test?

Thank you for your help. I've checked the drivers and they're correct, Java is updated, and the connector seems fine. When transferring the project to the CPU, everything works quickly. The delay only happens during online testing, and it varies—sometimes it's 1 second, other times up to 5, 6, or even 7 seconds.
That's a crucial detail. I apologize for possibly misguiding you earlier. I'm not sure what else to suggest.
Try using a different RS232-USB converter; some models can be quite unreliable.

Hi, check your COM port settings and try setting the Buffers to their minimum values. Make sure the driver matches your hardware. I use an FTDI USB-RS232 converter and it works well, even for older systems like Step5.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing long delays during online testing with [product_name] software version [version_no] when using a USB-to-RS232 converter. These delays do not occur when transferring projects, only during live monitoring, suggesting issues related to software, drivers, or hardware setup for online functionality. Potential causes discussed include driver compatibility, cable quality, and COM port configuration, but no definitive solution has been reached.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that online testing and monitoring with [product_name] software will be fast and reliable, similar to project transfer performance. They want the USB converter setup to enable smooth, real-time monitoring with the [product_name] CPU.
